MECHANICS LIEN WAIVER AND RELEASE FORMS (PROGRESS AND FINAL PAYMENT)
Prepared for Acme Construction, Inc. · Beta Builders, LLC

PURPOSE OF THIS DOCUMENT
California law prescribes four specific statutory forms that a claimant -- a contractor, subcontractor, supplier, or other person or entity furnishing labor, service, equipment, or material to a California work of improvement -- may use to waive and release mechanics lien, stop payment notice, and payment bond rights in exchange for payment: a Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment, an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment, a Conditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment, and an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment. This document reproduces the required statutory text of each of the four forms and states the statutory rules under which each form takes effect, becomes null and void, or fails to release the owner, construction lender, or payment bond surety. It does not itself tell any specific claimant, owner, contractor, or lender which of the four forms applies to their circumstances, when to sign one, or whether to accept one in exchange for a particular payment.

THESE STATUTORY WAIVER-AND-RELEASE RULES APPLY TO WORKS OF IMPROVEMENT
The waiver-and-release chapter of California's mechanics lien law -- the source of the four statutory forms in this document -- applies to a work of improvement governed by Part 6 (Works of Improvement) of Division 4 of the Civil Code, the same part of the Civil Code that governs preliminary notices, stop payment notices, payment bond claims, and mechanics liens on California private works.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The provisions of this chapter apply to a work of improvement governed by this part."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 8120, California Civil Code, applicability of the waiver-and-release chapter (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=8120.)
  Known gap: This clause states only that the waiver-and-release chapter applies to works of improvement governed by Part 6; it does not itself define "work of improvement" or identify which specific projects fall inside or outside Part 6's scope (for example, the boundary between private works covered by this part and public works, which are governed by a separate statutory scheme) -- those definitions appear in other Civil Code sections this document does not reproduce.

A CONTRACT CANNOT WAIVE ANOTHER CLAIMANT'S LIEN RIGHTS IN ADVANCE
An owner, direct contractor, or subcontractor cannot use a contract -- or any other means -- to waive, affect, or impair a different claimant's mechanics lien, stop payment notice, or payment bond rights in advance, whether or not that other claimant has notice of the attempt. A contract term that purports to do this is void and unenforceable, unless and until the affected claimant itself signs and delivers one of the statutory waiver and release forms.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An owner, direct contractor, or subcontractor may not, by contract or otherwise, waive, affect, or impair any other claimant’s rights under this part, whether with or without notice, and any term of a contract that purports to do so is void and unenforceable unless and until the claimant executes and delivers a waiver and release under this article."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 8122, California Civil Code, prohibition on advance third-party waiver of another claimant's rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=8122.)
  Known gap: This clause addresses only advance, third-party waiver attempts -- a contract clause by which an owner or contractor tries to waive a different claimant's rights on that claimant's behalf. It does not address a claimant's own voluntary waiver of its own rights using one of the four statutory forms reproduced elsewhere in this document, and it does not state what remedy (if any) the affected claimant has against the party who inserted the void contract term, a question this section does not answer.

WHEN A WAIVER AND RELEASE ACTUALLY PROTECTS THE OWNER, LENDER, OR SURETY
A claimant's signed waiver and release does not, by itself, release the owner, construction lender, or payment bond surety from a lien or claim. Two conditions must both be satisfied: the waiver and release must be in substantially the statutory form and signed by the claimant, and -- if the release is a conditional release -- there must also be evidence of payment to the claimant, which California law allows to be shown either by the claimant's endorsement on a single or joint payee check that has actually been paid by the bank it was drawn on, or by the claimant's own written acknowledgment of payment.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A claimant’s waiver and release does not release the owner, construction lender, or surety on a payment bond from a lien or claim unless both of the following conditions are satisfied:(a) The waiver and release is in substantially the form provided in this article and is signed by the claimant.(b) If the release is a conditional release, there is evidence of payment to the claimant. Evidence of payment may be either of the following:(1) The claimant’s endorsement on a single or joint payee check that has been paid by the financial institution on which it was drawn.(2) Written acknowledgment of payment by the claimant."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 8124, California Civil Code, conditions under which a waiver and release binds the owner, lender, or surety (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=8124.)
  Known gap: This clause states the statutory two-part test for when a release actually protects the owner, lender, or surety; it does not identify who bears the burden of proving evidence of payment in a lien-foreclosure or bond-claim dispute, and does not address what happens when a claimant signs an unconditional release without actually having been paid (that consequence, for the claimant rather than for the owner or lender, is addressed in the notice language of the unconditional forms themselves, reproduced in separate drafting clauses in this document). A CourtListener case-law search for judicial decisions construing Civil Code § 8124 was attempted for this document and returned an HTTP 429 rate-limit error (CourtListener's 125-request daily quota was exhausted) rather than search results, so this clause is based on statutory text alone and cites no case law.

WHEN THE CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON PROGRESS PAYMENT FORM IS REQUIRED
If a claimant is required to sign a waiver and release in exchange for, or to induce, a progress payment, and the claimant has not actually been paid in exchange for it (or is being given a single-payee or joint-payee check, rather than cash or a cleared payment, in exchange for it), the waiver and release is null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment form that California law sets out (reproduced in a companion drafting clause in this document).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "If a claimant is required to execute a waiver and release in exchange for, or in order to induce payment of, a progress payment and the claimant is not, in fact, paid in exchange for the waiver and release or a single payee check or joint payee check is given in exchange for the waiver and release, the waiver and release shall be null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the following form:"
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 8132, California Civil Code, when an unpaid conditional progress-payment waiver is void (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=8132.)
  Known gap: This clause describes only the trigger and consequence for the progress-payment conditional form under Civil Code § 8132; it does not address the separate, differently-worded rules for a final-payment waiver (covered in separate clauses below for Civil Code §§ 8136 and 8138), and it does not define what makes a waiver "substantially" in the statutory form for purposes of substantial compliance -- that phrase is used in the statute but not further defined by it.

CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON PROGRESS PAYMENT — STATUTORY FORM
CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON PROGRESS PAYMENT

NOTICE: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES THE CLAIMANT'S LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS EFFECTIVE ON RECEIPT OF PAYMENT. A PERSON SHOULD NOT RELY ON THIS DOCUMENT UNLESS SATISFIED THAT THE CLAIMANT HAS RECEIVED PAYMENT.

Identifying Information

Name of Claimant: Acme Construction, Inc.
Name of Customer: Beta Builders, LLC
Job Location: 123 Main St, Springfield
Owner: Jordan Alex Lee
Through Date: August 31, 2026

Conditional Waiver and Release

This document waives and releases lien, stop payment notice, and payment bond rights the claimant has for labor and service provided, and equipment and material delivered, to the customer on this job through the Through Date of this document. Rights based upon labor or service provided, or equipment or material delivered, pursuant to a written change order that has been fully executed by the parties prior to the date that this document is signed by the claimant, are waived and released by this document, unless listed as an Exception below. This document is effective only on the claimant's receipt of payment from the financial institution on which the following check is drawn:

Maker of Check: Beta Builders, LLC
Amount of Check: $15,000
Check Payable to: Acme Construction, Inc.

Exceptions

This document does not affect any of the following:
(1) Retentions.
(2) Extras for which the claimant has not received payment.
(3) The following progress payments for which the claimant has previously given a conditional waiver and release but has not received payment:
Date(s) of waiver and release: _______________________________________________
Amount(s) of unpaid progress payment(s): $_______________________________________________
(4) Contract rights, including (A) a right based on rescission, abandonment, or breach of contract, and (B) the right to recover compensation for work not compensated by the payment.

Signature

Claimant's Signature: _______________________________________________
Claimant's Title: _______________________________________________
Date of Signature: _______________________________________________

WHEN THE UNCONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON PROGRESS PAYMENT FORM IS REQUIRED
If a claimant is required to sign a waiver and release in exchange for, or to induce, a progress payment, and the waiver itself asserts that the claimant has, in fact, already been paid the progress payment, the waiver and release is null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment form that California law sets out, with the required "Notice to Claimant" warning printed in at least as large a type as the largest type otherwise used in the form.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "If the claimant is required to execute a waiver and release in exchange for, or in order to induce payment of, a progress payment and the claimant asserts in the waiver that the claimant has, in fact, been paid the progress payment, the waiver and release shall be null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the following form, with the text of the “Notice to Claimant” in at least as large a type as the largest"
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 8134, California Civil Code, validity and type-size requirements for the unconditional progress-payment waiver (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=8134.)
  Known gap: This clause covers only the unconditional progress-payment form's validity requirement and its type-size rule for the "Notice to Claimant" warning; the statute requires that warning to be printed in type at least as large as the largest type elsewhere in the form, but does not specify any particular point size, so this document cannot state a numeric minimum. It also does not address what recourse, if any, a claimant who signs this form without having actually been paid has against the party who obtained the unconditional release -- the form's own warning text (reproduced in the companion drafting clause) states only that the document remains enforceable against the claimant regardless.

UNCONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON PROGRESS PAYMENT — STATUTORY FORM
UNCONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON PROGRESS PAYMENT

NOTICE TO CLAIMANT: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES AND RELEASES LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS UNCONDITIONALLY AND STATES THAT YOU HAVE BEEN PAID FOR GIVING UP THOSE RIGHTS. THIS DOCUMENT IS ENFORCEABLE AGAINST YOU IF YOU SIGN IT, EVEN IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID. IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID, USE A CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE FORM.

Identifying Information

Name of Claimant: Acme Construction, Inc.
Name of Customer: Beta Builders, LLC
Job Location: 123 Main St, Springfield
Owner: Jordan Alex Lee
Through Date: August 31, 2026

Unconditional Waiver and Release

Rights based upon labor or service provided, or equipment or material delivered, pursuant to a written change order that has been fully executed by the parties prior to the date that this document is signed by the claimant, are waived and released by this document, unless listed as an Exception below. The claimant has received the following progress payment: $15,000

Exceptions

This document does not affect any of the following:
(1) Retentions.
(2) Extras for which the claimant has not received payment.
(3) Contract rights, including (A) a right based on rescission, abandonment, or breach of contract, and (B) the right to recover compensation for work not compensated by the payment.

Claimant's Title: _______________________________________________
Date of Signature: _______________________________________________

WHEN THE CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON FINAL PAYMENT FORM IS REQUIRED
If a claimant is required to sign a waiver and release in exchange for, or to induce, a final payment, and the claimant has not actually been paid in exchange for it (or is being given a single-payee or joint-payee check, rather than cash or a cleared payment, in exchange for it), the waiver and release is null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the Conditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment form that California law sets out.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "If the claimant is required to execute a waiver and release in exchange for, or in order to induce payment of, a final payment and the claimant is not, in fact, paid in exchange for the waiver and release or a single payee check or joint payee check is given in exchange for the waiver and release, the waiver and release shall be null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the following form:"
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 8136, California Civil Code, when an unpaid conditional final-payment waiver is void (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=8136.)
  Known gap: This clause mirrors the progress-payment conditional rule in Civil Code § 8132, but for final payment under § 8136 -- a textually separate section, not a subdivision of § 8132. Unlike the progress-payment forms, the final-payment forms reproduced in this document have no "Through Date" field and no exception for previously-waived-but-unpaid progress payments; the final-payment conditional form's Exceptions section instead covers only disputed claims for extras, a narrower carve-out this clause does not further explain.

CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON FINAL PAYMENT

NOTICE: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES THE CLAIMANT'S LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS EFFECTIVE ON RECEIPT OF PAYMENT. A PERSON SHOULD NOT RELY ON THIS DOCUMENT UNLESS SATISFIED THAT THE CLAIMANT HAS RECEIVED PAYMENT.

Identifying Information

Name of Claimant: Acme Construction, Inc.
Name of Customer: Beta Builders, LLC
Job Location: 123 Main St, Springfield
Owner: Jordan Alex Lee

Conditional Waiver and Release

This document waives and releases lien, stop payment notice, and payment bond rights the claimant has for labor and service provided, and equipment and material delivered, to the customer on this job. Rights based upon labor or service provided, or equipment or material delivered, pursuant to a written change order that has been fully executed by the parties prior to the date that this document is signed by the claimant, are waived and released by this document, unless listed as an Exception below. This document is effective only on the claimant's receipt of payment from the financial institution on which the following check is drawn:

Maker of Check: Beta Builders, LLC
Amount of Check: $15,000
Check Payable to: Acme Construction, Inc.

Exceptions

This document does not affect any of the following:
Disputed claims for extras in the amount of: $_______________________________________________

Signature

Claimant's Signature: _______________________________________________
Claimant's Title: _______________________________________________
Date of Signature: _______________________________________________

If a claimant is required to sign a waiver and release in exchange for, or to induce, a final payment, and the waiver itself asserts that the claimant has, in fact, already been paid the final payment, the waiver and release is null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the Unconditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment form that California law sets out, with the required "Notice to Claimant" warning printed in at least as large a type as the largest type otherwise used in the form.

citations.cite: California Civil Code, validity and type-size requirements for the unconditional final-payment waiver
citations.quote: If the claimant is required to execute a waiver and release in exchange for, or in order to induce payment of, a final payment and the claimant asserts in the waiver that the claimant has, in fact, been paid the final payment, the waiver and release shall be null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the following form, with the text of the “Notice to Claimant” in at least as large a type as the largest type

expectedJSON.gap: This clause states the validity and type-size requirement for the unconditional final-payment form under Civil Code § 8138, the last section in this waiver-and-release chapter; the chapter contains no sections numbered above 8138, so this document's coverage of the chapter (Civil Code §§ 8120-8138) is complete on its face, but this document does not address related sections outside this chapter -- for example, the separate rules governing a lien claimant's rights on a public work of improvement, or the mechanics lien claim and preliminary notice requirements covered in a separate document in this collection.

UNCONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE ON FINAL PAYMENT

NOTICE TO CLAIMANT: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES AND RELEASES LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS UNCONDITIONALLY AND STATES THAT YOU HAVE BEEN PAID FOR GIVING UP THOSE RIGHTS. THIS DOCUMENT IS ENFORCEABLE AGAINST YOU IF YOU SIGN IT, EVEN IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID. IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID, USE A CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE FORM.

Identifying Information

Name of Claimant: Acme Construction, Inc.
Name of Customer: Beta Builders, LLC
Job Location: 123 Main St, Springfield
Owner: Jordan Alex Lee

Unconditional Waiver and Release

This document waives and releases lien, stop payment notice, and payment bond rights the claimant has for all labor and service provided, and equipment and material delivered, to the customer on this job. Rights based upon labor or service provided, or equipment or material delivered, pursuant to a written change order that has been fully executed by the parties prior to the date that this document is signed by the claimant, are waived and released by this document, unless listed as an Exception below. The claimant has been paid in full.

Exceptions

This document does not affect the following:
Disputed claims for extras in the amount of: $_______________________________________________

Signature

Claimant's Title: _______________________________________________
